title: Toilet bowl fizz tablets
subtitle: Baking soda and citric acid tablets for weekly toilet cleaning
excerpt: Compressed baking soda and citric acid tablets that fizz in the toilet bowl, loosening deposits and deodorising. Scented with tea tree and eucalyptus essential oils. Drop one tablet in weekly. Makes about 12 tablets. Shelf life 6 months in an airtight jar.
sourceNotes: Fizzing action: sodium bicarbonate (pH ~8.3) + citric acid (pKa1 3.13) react when wet to release carbon dioxide, agitating the water and loosening light deposits. The mild acid environment from dissolved citric acid helps dissolve limescale (calcium carbonate). Tea tree EO (Melaleuca alternifolia) and eucalyptus EO (Eucalyptus globulus): broad-spectrum antimicrobial activity; effective at concentrations well below 1%. Binding without water: witch hazel or isopropanol added drop by drop as a binder, enough to allow pressing without premature fizzing. Storage critical: moisture triggers the acid-base reaction; airtight container essential.

recipe.batchNotes: Make a double batch and store in a wide-mouth airtight jar, 12 tablets is a 3-month supply at once-weekly use.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Set for 4 hours before moving to the storage jar. Keep the jar sealed to prevent humidity triggering the fizz reaction.
recipe.shelfLifeNotes: 6 months in an airtight jar. Exposure to humidity causes premature fizzing and clumping. If the tablets start to crumble or fizz when picked up, they've absorbed moisture and should be used quickly or discarded.

glossaryTerms.definition: A weak organic acid found in citrus fruit, available as a white powder. In these tablets, it reacts with bicarbonate of soda when wet to release carbon dioxide, producing the fizzing action.
A white or off-white deposit of calcium carbonate that forms when hard water evaporates on surfaces. The mildly acidic environment from dissolved citric acid helps dissolve it.

content.text: Combine the bicarbonate of soda, citric acid, and cornflour in a bowl. Stir to mix evenly.
Add the essential oils and stir in quickly.

Spritz the witch hazel into the mixture one spray at a time, stirring constantly between each spritz. Stop when the mixture just holds together when squeezed in your fist. If you add too much liquid at once, the mixture will fizz, spray in very small amounts.
Pack firmly into a silicone ice cube tray or small round moulds. Press down hard so the tablets compress. Leave to set for 4 hours.
Turn out carefully and transfer immediately to an airtight jar.
6 months in an airtight jar in a dry cupboard. Keep the jar away from the bathroom's steam, humidity degrades the tablets.
